title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodiction: a unifying classical variational principle
abstract: The same classical f-divergence admits inequivalent extensions to quantum states. The question is whether these extensions can be obtained from a common operational variational principle. Here we generalize Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization by introducing a reference prior state. More explicitly, we minimize the statistical distinguishability between a forward and a reverse prepare-and-measure process, related by retrodiction through the chosen reference and subject to prescribed quantum averages. Distinguishability is quantified by the classical f-divergence between their complete records. For faithful states in finite dimension, we prove that the same spectral implementation attains the minimum simultaneously for every operator-convex f. Varying the reference allows us to interpolate between standard and maximal quantum f-divergences of the prescribed states, passing through the geodesic family. More precisely, a flat reference yields the standard quantum f-divergences, thereby giving the Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions a variational characterization as optimal records. Choosing either prescribed state as reference recovers maximal quantum f-divergences and Matsumoto's reverse tests, while power references realize the geodesic interpolation. In the relative-entropy case, this gives the passage from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy by changing the prior for retrodiction.
summary: This paper unifies the study of quantum f-divergences by showing they can all be derived from a single variational principle based on comparing forward and reverse process records. By introducing a tunable reference prior state, the authors demonstrate a continuous path (geodesic) connecting various established quantum divergences. This provides a powerful, operational tool for characterizing quantum information measures.
main_problem: The paper seeks to determine if all quantum extensions of a classical f-divergence can be derived from a single, common operational variational principle.
main_result: Varying a reference prior state allows for a continuous interpolation between standard, maximal, and geodesic quantum f-divergences, providing a unified variational characterization.
method: The authors generalize Matsumoto's reverse-test optimization by minimizing the classical f-divergence between forward and reverse 'prepare-and-measure' process records, subject to quantum average constraints.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on quantum states (density operators) in a finite dimension, modeling preparation and measurement processes using weighted Positive Operator-Valued Measure (POVM) resolutions.
key_observables: The minimum statistical distinguishability, quantified by the classical f-divergence $D_f(R\|F)$, and the resulting quasi-entropy $V_f(ho, \sigma; \gamma)$.
important_parameters: The prescribed average states ($ho, \sigma, \gamma$), the choice of reference state ($\gamma$), and the operator-convex function $f$ defining the divergence.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes faithful states in finite dimension and that the record retains complete information to avoid trivial zero minima.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the admissible forward and reverse processes, while Figure 2 shows the reduction from two preparation channels to a single reverse test structure.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the minimum f-divergence for records, showing how varying the reference state interpolates between different quantum divergences (standard, maximal, geodesic), and finally extending the framework to include intermediate quantum channels.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep, operational variational framework for quantifying quantum distinguishability, which is fundamental to understanding quantum process characterization, resource theories, and information geometry in open quantum systems.
